title: Oncall alerts: add structured burn-rate payload + runbook/dashboard links
author: Miles Thornton
description: Context: As part of Tiered SLOs + error budgets, we’re rolling out burn-rate alerting. During the pilot we found that alerts landing in Slack/PagerDuty were missing: (1) a stable runbook link, (2) a dashboard deep-link scoped to the exact tier/service/region/model, and (3) enough structured context to let incident-bot enrich incident channels (budget scope, burn windows, tier, etc.) without scraping free-form text. This PR updates our oncall tooling integration to (a) require/runbook + dashboard annotations on burn-rate alerts, and (b) emit a structured payload to downstream consumers (PD, Slack notifier, incident-bot) so alerts are actionable and machine-readable. Changes: - Add a versioned JSON schema for alert payloads: "redwood_alert.v1" with fields for tier, service, slos/sli, budget_scope, region, route, model, burn_windows, and runbook/dashboard URLs. - Update alert routing pipeline to attach runbook_url + slo_dashboard_url via alert annotations and validate presence for burn-rate alerts (warn-only for 2 weeks, then enforce). - Extend PagerDuty event enrichment to include custom_details with the structured payload (no customer identifiers; only internal dimensions). - Update Slack notifier formatting to show Tier + SLO name + burn window + links (Runbook, Dashboard, Error budget policy). - Add unit tests + golden fixtures for burn-rate alerts (hosted + dedicated) and ensure no PII/customer_id is ever included. Rollout plan: - Start with burn-rate alerts only (alertname matches /BurnRate/ or has annotation redwood.alert_type=error_budget_burn). - Validation is "warn" (log + metric) for 2 weeks; enforcement toggle is config-driven: ONCALL_ALERT_ENFORCE_RUNBOOK_ANNOTATIONS=false by default in prod. - After docs + runbooks are updated, SRE will flip enforcement for #eng-sre owned rules first. Links: - Linear: ENG-2420 (burn-rate alerts), ENG-2426 (oncall playbooks). - Internal support: INT-1188 (alert routing updates). Testing: - Unit tests for payload schema validation (go test ./... in services/oncall). - Integration test fixture for PD event mapping. - Manual: fired a synthetic burn-rate alert in staging; verified Slack message includes Runbook + Dashboard links; verified PD incident contains custom_details.redwood_alert_v1.

alert-router: attach runbook/dashboard annotations and generate structured payload
pagerduty: include custom_details.redwood_alert_v1 (sanitized) for burn-rate alerts
slack-notifier: update formatting to include tier + burn windows + deep links
tests: golden fixtures for hosted/dedicated burn-rate alerts + schema validation cases
docs: add annotation requirements for burn-rate alerts (warn-only rollout)

conversation: Sean Gallagher (reviewer): We should be strict about not emitting any customer identifiers in PD custom_details. Some of the dedicated alerts currently carry customer_slug in labels. Are we redacting/omitting? Miles Thornton (author): Good catch. I added a sanitizer that drops any label keys matching /(customer|tenant|org|account)/i and a unit test covering customer_slug + tenant_id. Also updated the mapper to only allowlist specific keys into custom_details (tier/service/region/route/model/slo_name/burn_windows/urls). Allison Grant (reviewer): +1 on schema versioning. Can you make the schema explicit about required vs optional fields? Specifically runbook_url should be required for burn-rate alerts once enforcement flips. Miles Thornton (author): Updated schema.go to distinguish required fields for burn-rate payloads and added a config gate (ONCALL_ALERT_ENFORCE_RUNBOOK_ANNOTATIONS) so we can ramp. In warn-only mode we emit a metric oncall_missing_runbook_url_total{alertname=...}. Caleb Johnson (reviewer): Does the dashboard link include high-cardinality params? We shouldn’t be generating links that explode cardinality or embed huge query strings. Miles Thornton (author): The link builder uses a fixed set of filters and only includes tier/service/region plus optional model/route when present AND on an allowlist (route is normalized group, not raw path). Also clamps model to Redwood catalog name (no customer-provided strings). Added tests for normalization. Dev Patel (reviewer): For Support escalation, can the Slack message include the error budget policy link as well? This helps oncall decide comms quickly. Miles Thornton (author): Added a third link in Slack attachments: "Policy" pointing to the error budget policy page. Also included it in PD custom_details as policy_url. Sergio Costa (reviewer): Nit: Please keep the existing Slack layout for non-burn alerts. Also the alertname matching is a bit fragile; prefer annotation-driven routing. Miles Thornton (author): Updated routing to primarily key off annotation redwood.alert_type=error_budget_burn, with alertname regex as fallback for legacy rules. Non-burn alerts unchanged. Sean Gallagher (reviewer): Looks good. Please add a note in docs about the 2-week warn-only period and who owns flipping enforcement. Miles Thornton (author): Added to docs/oncall/alert-annotations.md and included SRE owners (#eng-sre) plus link to ENG-2420 rollout checklist. Approvals: Sean Gallagher ✅, Allison Grant ✅, Caleb Johnson ✅, Dev Patel ✅, Sergio Costa ✅. Merged via squash.
release_notes: - Burn-rate alerts now include Runbook + Dashboard deep links and a structured redwood_alert.v1 payload for downstream automation (Slack/PD/incident-bot). - Runbook annotation enforcement is gated and defaults to warn-only in prod until SRE flips the toggle post-migration.
